title: Parental Rights in Dependency Court
statement: Unless there are aggravated circumstances, you are entitled to services to help you reunify with your child.
source_says: the child's mother and statutorily presumed father or guardians
steps: Opened the cited statute on public.law, rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov, the Self-Help Guide for parents and the Judicial Council booklet PDF with the fetch tool and asked for exact quotes. WIC 361.5(a) orders services when a child is removed, for the mother and presumed father or guardians; a biological father gets them only if the court finds they will benefit the child. 361.5(b) says 'Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision' and lists 17 situations. The words 'aggravated circumstances' are not in the section.
fix: If your child is removed, the judge must order services to help you get your child back in most cases. The law lists 17 serious situations where the judge can say no to services. If you are a father the court has not yet named a presumed parent, the judge may order services but does not have to.

statement: You have the right to appeal court decisions you disagree with.
source_says: An order by the court that a hearing pursuant to this section be held is not appealable at any time
steps: Opened the cited statute on public.law, rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov, the Self-Help Guide for parents and the Judicial Council booklet PDF with the fetch tool and asked for exact quotes. title: The Jurisdiction Hearing
statement: You do not have to prove you are innocent.
source_says: The presumption created by subdivision (a) constitutes a presumption affecting the burden of producing evidence.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 334, 355, 355.1, 356, 358, rules 5.682 and 5.684 on courts.ca.gov, the Self-Help Guide for parents and the Judicial Council booklet with the fetch tool and asked for exact quotes. WIC 355(a) puts proof on the side asking for the finding. But WIC 355.1(a) says certain findings 'shall be prima facie evidence that the minor is a person described by subdivision (a), (b), or (d)' of Section 300, and 355.1(d) covers a parent 'previously convicted of sexual abuse'. In those cases the parent must bring evidence to answer the presumption.
fix: In most cases you do not have to prove anything. The county has to prove its claims. In a few cases, like some serious injuries to a child, the law lets the judge assume the claim is true unless you bring evidence against it. Ask your lawyer if that applies to you.
